content.text: The problem is in the these lines:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export-verify/blob/master/verify.py#L225-L226

If you parse the data directly with rdflib, the graphs are correctly interpreted as equivalent, but if you pass the response data to the parser with 'data=response.text', the graphs are interpreted as different. This must have to do with how unicode escapes are encoded/decoded during the handling of this data.

Did I understand you to say that this problem occurs only when trying to verify an import?  Or does it happen for both exports and imports?  I ask because I have a couple of objects on my workstation that include Cyrillic and Chinese characters.  If I run an export and verify the export, they seem to verify fine.

, it is possible that I could have said that.  But I've also subsequently seen issues on exports.  I have some newspapers where there are non-ASCII quotation marks that seem to get evaluated as different when comparing triples.
But all of this needs more research.  Any additional testing of various scenarios with content that pushes the boundaries of things we have tried will be helpful.

Well, as I've said, I haven't seen issues verifying exports of a couple of objects that contain Cyrillic and Chinese characters.  I don't know enough about Unicode to say for sure exactly how these characters are encoded, except that I believe they are UTF-8.  When I look at them in a web browser using the Fedora API, or indexed in Solr by Hydra, or in the export .ttl file, I just see them as Cyrillic or Chinese characters.  Not sure how my experience relates to the issues you've seen, though.
Forgot to add ... if you'll share the sample dataset that you made for youn with me, I can see if I see the same errors.
As I noted on IRC, I downloaded the 4.7.2 single item backup, restored it, exported it, and ran the verification tool with no verification failures.
: My results were the same as Jim's. I uploaded the csv output from verification to the team drive.
I thought I would download the Fedora 4.6.0 one-click, restore

's 4.6.0 backup, export, and see if I can replicate the verification errors he encountered.  Then, I guess a decision needs to be made about how to proceed.  E.g., do we try to pinpoint more precisely the Fedora versions which do / do not encounter this problem?  do we try to determine the exact nature of the issue with exports from earlier versions of Fedora?  etc.  The simplest answer might be just to say something like the following in the tool's README: "The verification tool is known to work correctly on exports from Fedora 4.7.2 but has been observed to flag potentially spurious mismatches related to Unicode-escaped characters on exports from certain earlier versions of Fedora (e.g., 4.6.0)."
: I suspect some documentation in the README along the lines you suggested would be sufficient for this ticket.

: I agree with Jim's assessment. It would be good to follow up on this some more and try to pinpoint the problem, but I'm not sure that there is going to be enough production use of the verification tool with 4.6 Fedoras to warrant a lot of time investigating the specific cause.  A simple note in the README might be best.

The other element at play here is that I'm not quite sure that we have identified the cause of all the permutations of this issue.  The original bug came up during the third import-export sprint and was definitely associated with unicode-escaped characters in the RDF that was being written to disk by the exporter.  I will attempt to recreate that behavior today and confirm whether it is also only found in the 4.6 version, or whether that can be demonstrated in 4.7.2. The effect was the same, but the apparent cause was slightly different.

I brought 4.6.0 one-click on my workstation and created an object with various non-Roman / non-ASCII characters.  Exported and ran verification tool.  Verification tool reported a triples mismatch, which is consistent with

's experience with an export from 4.6.0.  Going to bring up 4.7.2 one-click, create the same object, export, and run the verification tool.  Will report on the results – I'm expecting no verification mismatches.
As expected, verification of export from 4.7.2 containing same characters as above did not result in a triples mismatch.
: Thanks very much for running these tests. I agree that a note in the README for the verification tool might be best. Would you like to add the note, or should I? Thanks!!
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export-verify/pull/28

The issue was determined to be at least in part specific to fcrepo 4.6.0, and could not be reproduced in 4.7.2.  It was agreed that an update to the documentation of the verification tool would be a good first step. This update was completed with
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export-verify/commit/bc57af2f08ee24cdbc47afb6e91af83cd4dd34f4
This ticket should remain open for the time being until we determine whether any version of this sort of error can be shown to exist in 4.7.2.

The attached backup contains a resource with a title in various alternate scripts. The title is not Unicode escaped in the repository nor in the export. The verification tool generates an error on Book1.ttl even though its checksum is identical to checksums generated on metadata retrieved via the RESTful HTTP API from the original repository and the restored repository.
MD5 (Book1_fcrepo4-data-4.6.0_REST.ttl) = 68335703b83bb7de66c57065fb511a56
MD5 (Book1_fcrepo4-data-4.6.0-restore_REST.ttl) = 68335703b83bb7de66c57065fb511a56
MD5 (fcrepo4-data-4.6.0-restore-export/rest/Collection1/Book1.ttl) = 68335703b83bb7de66c57065fb511a56

The attached backup was created from and restored to a 4.7.3-RC repository using the one-click jar. It contains a resource with a title in various alternate scripts. The title is not Unicode escaped in the repository nor in the export. The verification tool does not generate any errors.
Thanks,
, for doing all this great legwork. This would appear to confirm that the other 'flavor' of this problem is also specific to the 4.6 line.
I have not been able to reproduce the problem encountered earlier with escapes in serialized resources using the 4.7.2 version of fcrepo.
I think that these two commits:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export-verify/commit/bc57af2f08ee24cdbc47afb6e91af83cd4dd34f4
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export-verify/commit/382c95b948104987fda9a537f548b7a9658d0fc5

together with the research and testing that went on around them, are sufficient for us to consider this issue resolved.  The problem seems to be limited to fcrepo v4.6 and its underlying Modeshape version.
This issue has been reviewed and tested and can be closed (the PRs above solve the problem).

The import-export verification tool, when encountering unicode-escaped characters in an RDF document serialized to disk, fails to translate the characters in a way that allows it to recognize the same triples coming from Fedora.
It seems like the tool ought to be able to make the necessary transformation to recognize that the two resources are equivalent.
